rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning God's limits, the commentary moves from the implied promise to their keepers and the threat to violators to detail punishment and reassure believers of victory.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر حدوده , ولوح بالعطف على غير معطوف عليه إلى بشارة حافظها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يحادون means persistently contending against God in denial and trying to replace His limits; the wording covers even concealed opposition.
rows.anchor: أي يغالبون الملك الأعلى على جحوده ليجعلوا حدودا غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an example of hidden opposition, the author describes unionists who literalize ambiguous verses and thereby unsettle clear rulings and the whole law.
rows.anchor: كمحادة أهل الاتحاد الذين يتبعون المتشابه فيجرونه على ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كَبتوا means they were thrown down, defeated, broken, humiliated, and disgraced, with their aims frustrated.
rows.anchor: أي صرعوا وكباو لوجوههم وكسروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense presents their defeat as certain, as though its judgment were already completed.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالماضي إشارة إلى تحقق وقوعه والفراغ من قضائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier opponents include Noah's people and later groups who persisted in disobedience and refused evidence or proof.
rows.anchor: كقوم نوح ومن بعدهم ممن أصر على العصيان

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says that whoever neglects a Prophetic Sunna and introduces an innovation in religion joins this group and incurs its humiliation.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : ومن ضيع لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سنة وأحدث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear signs establish this warning and everything needed for faith and for abandoning opposition to God's limits.
rows.anchor: دلالات عظيمة هي في غاية البيان لذلك ولكل ما يتوقف عليه الإيمان بترك المحادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those firmly committed to disbelief and altering God's commands face punishment that humiliates them and strips away their pride.
rows.anchor: يهينهم ذلك العذاب ويذهب عزهم وشماختهم ويتركون به محادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment comes when God restores the explicitly mentioned disbelievers and the implicitly included believers to life, all gathered together.
rows.anchor: في وقت إعادة الملك الأعظم للكافرين المصرح بهم والمؤمنين المشار إليه أحياء كما كانوا { جميعا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will inform them fully and exhaustively of their deeds, exposing them and establishing the proof against them.
rows.anchor: أي يخبرهم إخبارا عظيما مستقصى { بما عملوا } إخزاء لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has encompassed every deed in number, quality, time, and place, while people forgot the immense total and forgot sins through heedlessness.
rows.anchor: أحاط به عددا كما وكيفا وزمانا ومكانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their disregard of forgotten sins is itself disregard and audacity toward God.
rows.anchor: ونسوا ما فيه المعاصي تهاونا بها , وذلك عين التهاون بالله والاجتراء عليه

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says that recalling a sin during judgment brings such shame and regret that it eclipses every punishment; believers should obey, and if they slip, remember the sin and pray earnestly.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : إذا حوسب أحد في القيامة على عمل عمله تصور له ما فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is present, watchful, and preserving over absolutely everything; His encompassing, overpowering witness ensures perfect keeping.
rows.anchor: حفيظ حاضر لا يغيب , ورقيب لا يفعل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr argues that the world glorifies God by its state and testifies to its dependence on a wise maker unlike His creation.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما نزه سبحانه نفسه عن تقول الملحدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continuing Ibn al-Zubayr's argument, the sequence moves from the universe's praise in 57:1 to God's address to believers in 57:7, a shift in address.
rows.anchor: 77 ( { سبح لله ما في السماوات والأرض } ) 77

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr compares this shift with al-Baqara: after classifying people, the discourse invites all humanity to worship, then turns to the Prophet about the angels.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك ضرب من الالتفات , والواقع هنا منه أشبه بقوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr traces a sequence from rebuking Arab polytheists through the warnings of al-Qamar and al-Rahman to the afterlife in al-Waqiʿa, then God's transcendence and believers' address in al-Hadid.
rows.anchor: غالب آيها جار على ذلك ومجدد له أولها سورة ( ص ) كما نبه عليه في سورة القمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says that after accounts of past peoples, creation, the afterlife, duties, and recompense are completed, later discourse chiefly turns to believers' rulings and salvation.
rows.anchor: فلما كمل ذلك صرف الكلام إلى ما يخص المؤمنين في أحكامهم وتعريفهم بما فيه من خلاصهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining the distribution of fay and warning about the difficulty of accepting it, the text specifies its recipients, the central purpose of the allocation.
rows.anchor: وبين مصرف الفيء من القرى , وتهدد في المخالفة في ذلك لصعوبته على النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: للفقراء is either a substitute for the recipients beginning with God and the Messenger, since aid for the emigrants is for their sake, or an answer to an implied question about the allocation; it cannot substitute for ذي القربى lest it restrict the gift to needy relatives.
rows.anchor: فقال مبدلا من { الله وللرسول } وما عطف عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emigrants were genuinely poor: some bound a stone to the belly from hunger and used a dugout for winter shelter after losing former wealth.
rows.anchor: الذي كان الإنسان منهم يعصب الحجر على بطنه من الجوع ويتخذ الحفرة في الشتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author specifies the poor as emigrants because hijra can mean leaving unbelievers without leaving one's homeland; the passive أخرجوا foregrounds expulsion rather than the identity of the expeller.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت الهجرة قد تطلق على من هجر أهل الكفر من غير مفارقة الوطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expulsion here implies deprivation, and mentioning property evokes wealth as a person's shelter or container.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن المال السترة للإنسان لأنه ظرف له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Losing worldly possessions is not a defect when it comes from God, nor does it impair sincerity; the Banu Nadir outcome fulfilled the emigrants' hope.
rows.anchor: ولما كان غلب الدنيا من النقائص , بين أنه إذا كان من الله لم يكن كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favor encompasses this world, religion, and the hereafter, and enriches the emigrants so they need no one else.
rows.anchor: من الدنيا والدين والآخرة فيغنيهم بفضله عمن سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enables them to do what pleases Him; seeking His reward does not spoil sincerity, and He brings them to the abode of honor.
rows.anchor: يوفقهم لما يرضيه عنهم ولا يجعل رغبتهم في العوض منه قادحا في الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They continually support God and His Messenger with their lives and property so that Satan's party is overcome.
rows.anchor: على سبيل التجديد في كل وقت والاستمرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their migration and severing of hostile ties prove their sincere faith: they oppose God's and the Messenger's enemies and support their allies, even those far away.
rows.anchor: دل على كمال صدقهم فيما ادعوه من الإيمان بالله ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The religion is established by clear proofs through steadfastness in trials, and divine help may arrive in proportion to affliction; God gave the emigrants Banu Nadir property.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن مبنى الدين على إقامة البينات بالثبات عن الابتلاءات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After praising the emigrants and satisfying them with their allocation, the discourse praises the Ansar to console and thank them.
rows.anchor: أتبعه مدحهم جبرا لهم وشكرا لصنيعهم فقال عاطفا على مجموع القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ansar made the city their settled home: it had been prepared for migration and victory, was their lasting place of residence, and was not a place to abandon for its blessing.
rows.anchor: أي جعلوا بغاية جهدهم { الدار } الكاملة في الدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author construes settling faith as keeping its company and holding fast to it as to a home one cannot do without.
rows.anchor: ولابسوه وصحبوه وخصوه بالصحبة ولزموه لزوما هو كلزوم المنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate parsing treats faith as an attribute of the city: the conjunction marks firm possession of both qualities, and the city is called faith because faith is established and spreads from there.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الإيمان وصفا للدار بإعادة العاطف للإشارة إلى التمكن في كل من الوصفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ansar stayed in the city out of love for faith, not for their property: faith's honor and public strength were fully realized there, otherwise they would have gone wherever the Prophet settled.
rows.anchor: لأجل أن أموالهم بها بل محبة في الإيمان علما منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من قبلهم means before the emigrants' migration, not the whole period since the Messenger's mission; the Ansar had already joined settled faith to settled residence.
rows.anchor: أي قبل هجرة المهاجرين لأن وصفهم بالهجرة لم يكن إلا بعد إيجادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their settled faith before the emigrants arrived is a complete virtue: the emigrants only later combined faith and residence through migration.
rows.anchor: فالأنصار جمعوا التمكن في الإيمان إلى التمكن في الدار من قبل أن يجمع المهاجرون بينهما بالهجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ansar continually renew their love for everyone who migrates to them.
rows.anchor: أخبر عنهم بقوله : { يحبون } أي على سبيل التجديد والاستمرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate parsing coordinates this clause with المهاجرين and makes it a circumstantial clause, thereby assigning the description jointly.
rows.anchor: وقيل العطف على المهاجرين , وهذه حال فيكون هذا حكما بالمشاركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destination phrase heightens the emigrants' claim on the Ansar: choosing them as their destination itself shows great love.
rows.anchor: لأن القصد إلى الإنسان يوجب حقه عليه لأنه لولا كمال محبته له ما خصه بالقصد إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the Ansar's sharing of their homes and wealth, and even offering to share their wives, as visible proof of their love; the emigrants declined the latter and accepted wealth.
rows.anchor: شاطروا المهاجرين في أموالهم وعرضوا عليهم أن يشاطروهم نساءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They feel no need in their hearts, still less do they voice a request for what the emigrants received.
rows.anchor: التي هي مساكن قلوبهم فتصدر منها أوامر القلوب فضلا عن أن تنطق ألسنتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حاجة names the cause, need, in place of its result, asking for the emigrants' allocation.
rows.anchor: وكان الحامل على طلب ذلك الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The allocation includes fay and any other gift, whoever gave it, even God and His Messenger; lacking a reason to ask makes envy or resentment still less likely.
rows.anchor: من الفيء وغيره من أموال بني النضير وغيرهم من أي مؤت كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse strongly encourages brotherhood and warns against envy and resentment.
rows.anchor: فهذه الآية من أعظم حاث على حسن الإخاء محذر من الحسد والاستياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يؤثرون means choosing the best things for others and giving them preferentially, whoever the recipient may be.
rows.anchor: يوقعون الأثرة وهي اختيار الأشياء الحسنة لغيرهم تخصيصا لهم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They prefer others over themselves; the author takes naming the self as evidence that they are thoroughly free of base traits.
rows.anchor: وذكر النفس دليل على أنهم في غاية النزاهة من الرذائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خصاصة is poverty, a serious gap or need surrounding them, from the gaps in a building.
rows.anchor: أي فقر وخلل في الأحوال وحاجة شديدة تحيط بهم من كل جانب , من خصائص البناء وهي فرجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive يُوقَ signals that overcoming the soul's vice is difficult and requires strong divine aid.
rows.anchor: وكان علاج الرذائل صعبا جدا , لا يطيقه الإنسان إلا بمعونة من الله شديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protection from the soul's avarice means not withholding what one has and not coveting another's property out of envy.
rows.anchor: فلا يكون مانعا لما عنده , حريصا على ما عند غيره حسدا

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar defines avarice as a man's eye aspiring to what is not his.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عمر رضي الله عنه : الشح أن تطمح عين الرجل فيما ليس له

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet warns that avarice destroyed earlier peoples by driving them to shed blood and violate what was forbidden.
rows.anchor: اتقوا الشح فإنه أهلك من كان قبلكم , حملهم على أن سفكوا دماءهم واستحلو محارمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those purified from base traits are the truly elevated and fully successful, attaining every desired good.
rows.anchor: أي الكاملون في الفوز بكل مراد

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says a heart freed from attachments and possessions characterizes spiritual masters; one captive to worldly stakes remains preoccupied with transactions and demanding people's due, without tasting the spiritual path.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : وتجرد القلب من الأعراض والأملاك صفة السادة والأكابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the emigrants arrived, the Ansar divided homes and property with them; after Banu Nadir's fay, the Prophet offered either a shared division while migrants stayed in Ansar homes, or the Banu Nadir property with the migrants leaving.
rows.anchor: وشرح الآية أن الأنصار كانوا لما قدم عليهم المهاجرون قسموا دورهم وأموالهم بينهم وبينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ansar chose to give the Banu Nadir allocation to the emigrants while they remained in the Ansar's homes; another version has them also offer a share of their own property.
rows.anchor: بل يقسم بين المهاجرين خاصة ويكونون في دورنا كما كانوا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed for mercy upon the Ansar and their children.
rows.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( اللهم ارحم الأنصار

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr praised the Ansar and thanked them for their generosity.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه : جزاكم الله خيرا يا معشر الأنصار

rows.speaker: العنزي
rows.claim: Al-ʿAnazi's poem compares the Ansar's support to rescuing companions when their footing slipped, and says they would have tired of the burden only if they had suffered the same hardship.
rows.anchor: كما قال العنزي : جزى الله عنا جعفرا حين أزلقت بنا نعلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: العزيز is irresistible in victory: no defeated opponent can resist, escape, or frustrate Him; all depend on Him continually, and none can thwart His judgment or vengeance.
rows.anchor: والعزة غلبة لا يجد معها المغلوب وجه مدافعة وجه مدافعة ولا انفلات ولا إعجاز

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali defines العزيز as one whose like is rare, who is urgently needed, and whom it is difficult to reach.
rows.anchor: قال الغزالي : وهو الذي يقل وجود مثله وتشتد الحاجة إليه ويصعب الوصول إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's name al-ʿAziz is often joined to verses of fulfilled rulings alongside wisdom and knowledge, signaling justice.
rows.anchor: ولذلك ينظم كثير بآيات إمضاء الأحكام متصلا بالحكمة والعلم إنباء عن العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Jabbar is the mighty one beyond the reach of resistance, who rectifies the affairs of whomever He wills and compels creation to His will.
rows.anchor: وهو العظيم الذي يفوت المقاوم مناله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root evokes a superior compelling an inferior while remaining inaccessible to the inferior's attempts; nothing leaves God's grasp and none reaches Him except as He permits.
rows.anchor: ما يحاول مناله منه الأدنى مع الظهور التام الذي تدور مادته عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creation is too weak to disobey God even momentarily without His will, and nothing escapes His grasp.
rows.anchor: فهم أحقر من أن يعصوه طرفة عين بغير إرادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited report has Hell continue asking whether there is more until God places His foot in it; the author says this humiliates Hell, since the foot is a site of humiliation.
rows.anchor: حتى يضع الجبار فيها قدمه أي يهينها فإن القدم موضع الإهانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes visible sovereignty through outward powers as mulk, inward sovereignty through hidden powers as malakut, and God's exclusive dominion beyond both as jabarut.
rows.anchor: فله الملك ظهورا بالأيدي الظاهرة من الإنسان وما دونه , وله الملكوت بطونا بالأيدي الباطنة من الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutakabbir covers outward and inward compulsion: God's majesty shows creation its smallness, His independence, and their dependence on Him.
rows.anchor: ليعم الإلجاء الظاهر والباطن فالكبرياء جملة تأدي أمر الله وظاهر خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creatures are equally small before God's power and have no rightful share in pride; this name belongs uniquely to Him.
rows.anchor: لسواء الخلق في عام حضرة القدرة شملهم الصغر فلم يصح منهم كبر , ولا شرع لهم تكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The display of God's outward and inward dominion establishes that He is exalted above every defect, especially association with partners.
rows.anchor: أنتج ذلك تعاليه عن شوب نقص لا سيما بالشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partners are created things, idols and others, great or small, in heaven or on earth.
rows.anchor: أي من هذه المخلوقات من الأصنام وغيرهما مما في الأرض أو في السماء من كبير وصغير . وجليل وحقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof of oneness from God's majesty concludes, then a second proof begins by moving through levels from the hiddenest to the hidden and then the manifest.
rows.anchor: ولما تم دليل الوحدانية بما حل من التفهيم بالتدني إلى الملك ثم بالتعلي إلى التكبر فأنتج هذه الخاتمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The new proof starts with faith in the unseen; leaving that ground leads to ruin.
rows.anchor: إعلاما بأنه لا براح عن الإيمان بالغيب , ومن برح عنه هلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one but God truly merits the pronoun: He exists through Himself, whereas every other possible being might not exist.
rows.anchor: أي الذي لا شيء يستحق أن يطلق عليه هذا الضمير غيره لأن وجوده من ذاته ولا شيء غيره إلا وهو ممكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah is the most familiar, true name with no namesake and no equal.
rows.anchor: الذي ليس له سمي فلا كفوء له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author begins a proof from creation: the true creator assigns each thing its measure, like a shoemaker marking a boundary and size on leather before cutting and shaping it.
rows.anchor: كالحاذي يخلق أي يقدر في الجلد حدا وقدرا لنعل ونحوه
